details: The change preserves the original exact panel target and adds a separate reopenPanel callback, leaving activatePanel as the existing CDP-only operation for callers whose owned root page may have navigated.

Authenticated Scrape invokes reopenPanel after member authentication and organization verification, inside resourceAction, before the pre-existing native document.visibilityState gate and before viewport measurement or cases.

The opener foregrounds the owned root page, clears stale result text, uses the existing real trusted #open-panel click and FRONTEND_RPC openPanel route, requires a fresh nonempty reply with ok=true and result.opened=true, then activates the original exact target.

This addresses the observed harness omission (activation can focus a hidden SIDE_PANEL without reopening it) without changing identity assertions, exact extension/SIDE_PANEL context checks, auth/storage checks, or resource health gates.
The prior run 37241717888 remains valid failure evidence: member/org passed, one exact target and context remained, panel was hidden despite focus, and zero cases ran. It does not test this repair.
verdict_a.changed_condition_native_run: Run one fresh native authenticated Scrape acceptance with member mode and a verified organization against the repaired pushed head/artifact. Preserve exact artifact/extension identity and existing auth, organization, context, and resource gates. The changed boundary must now report visible and continue to viewport measurement and Scrape cases; if it fails, retain the new run report and diagnostic. No guest-only run establishes the changed member/OAuth condition.

verdict_b.quality: source repair and lightweight guard are sound within their stated boundary; browser/runtime behavior remains unproven
verdict_b.sibling_callers: The helper is exposed only as a new callback. Existing activatePanel behavior and non-Scrape native callers remain unchanged. Scrape uses the root owned page before its fixture navigation; member OAuth's web page is closed before return per the existing flow.
verdict_b.resource_and_lifecycle: Reopen is charged through resourceAction and followed by the existing requireResourceHealth. Existing original target attachment and final detach/owned-child cleanup remain in place. The helper does not close or create a browser, profile, or extension target.
verdict_b.privacy: The helper includes the RPC reply JSON in its thrown refusal error. This mirrors the existing initial-open path's error format and currently expected replies contain only open status/reason, so I found no new demonstrated disclosure; fixed-code refusal diagnostics would be safer if RPC payloads can carry arbitrary fields.
verdict_b.guard_limits: The new node:test checks success/refusal/no-fresh-reply behavior and executes the actual authenticated Scrape setup prefix with external auth/browser dependencies doubled. Its visibility predicate is simulated; it cannot prove Chromium reopened the attached target, and the source-slice seam is deliberately narrower than full native integration.
verdict_b.no_findings: No identity, authorization, exact-context, or resource gate was weakened in the reviewed diff.

limits: No browser, workflow dispatch, release, product change, inventory mutation, or child agent used in this review.
CI and a changed-condition native member run were not run here.
The pre-existing unrelated dirty workspace report was left untouched.
